# Election update: Thursday, November 5 (morning)

## Bottom line
The House results table now marks 391 of 435 races called: D 244, R 147, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). Counting 2 more races news outlets report as called, it is D 244, R 149. NBC News's results page headlines Democrats winning House control ([NBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMibkFVX3lxTE1zb3FDMGdwaC1OZmxSWVh1cThkeDRQcVlLaFh2NUg1WlJuX19CMV82aHJrajJvM3RrZGpmeHMyWjRzcXptN1V2NWVSb2F0OVZUc19tSXNjb1EyaUgxcmtOeFJhdlJZU3Bob0JWb2xn?oc=5)). In the Senate, Democrats have secured 54 seats to Republicans' 44, counting seats not up, with 51 needed ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Alaska and Mississippi are still uncalled ([CNN](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxNMmx1N2JlVTE0Y2M0YldEeEtmT1pZR3BPRFc5TW1QcVF0RnAyZlUxd2lXYUhVWk9EQ1BUSmV3amFncDlVYnUtRmhpekF3RFpVMXUzeEFYaHA1WFppclJQeVJCRWNveHE1V2VLb21Jal9JaHBqZ3FnRnprSmtyZmpoRw?oc=5)). No seat rated safe is within 5 points.

## Recounts and certification
- **Florida:** FL-27's margin falls within the automatic machine recount, per the Miami-Dade supervisor of elections ([WPLG](https://news.google.?oc=5)). The Palm Beach Post explains when Florida certifies ([Palm Beach Post](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Mississippi:** Hinds County expects certification to take several days after historic turnout ([WLBT](https://news.google.?oc=5)). ABC News explains the state's recount options ([ABC](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **North Carolina:** WUNC explains what comes next for 10 close contests ([WUNC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxQM2xmLWJWWmJYbUJxUm05RC1RU1NfSFc5VWNfOHRDQ3ZkTF9ISS1pNW1xSG5HenFfMDVTaEJoNlgydEtSc1hUbm1wTXUwNGN5S0hqSlo5cWo5YUtRRGcxblg2anMzREVPOEZKemNqRGZsSmN6SUUtZ0dZVTlBbXM1cVQ1T0FvbDVKNXMwM2hNNmFiX0xEa0ZsTDZRaWMxWTZVbHlkcQ?oc=5)).
- **Nationally:** WBAL reports 16 midterm races within 1 point ([WBAL](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxNa1FpMmRsU2lDeFVlTWxDZEozNDRQaGlNTnJiN3Z5QWJIWnlyX2dMTTRfSGdDNENHS2ZwbFM1MF9Ib0lINWdZTU9IMXhfdzlWcGRNeUFfZGZQakVaZ0J0c3hEV1NNRjNLTjQ5TWZSYjg2dzQ3SFN5bXlBQ1o4N0gza3ViRENBdThsWG9jbHFqSEFqcHRFLUhZ?oc=5)).

## Legal and federal action
- **Alaska:** ABC News reported on Election Day that President Trump told DOJ to sue to block the Senate result if the Republican narrowly loses ([ABC](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Separately, a federal judge dismissed a Trump attempt to intervene in the race, NBC News reported Nov. 2 ([NBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxQbFlaVlhKRUJyMGFkM0w1dEJOQzFHYWw1RThkczBNTlVVWGVrU3ZfNFR1UjNoelNmY0M0YkJrdmM0WnVidVMzQ21tOVZvNm5ONnJZUEJySjhIMjZnclFwSUJheWozSG1xU1Bnc2QzeEZHOThDekZYR2tLbW5yajFqOXFmU3pHOFVWeU05ZWljbmVSN1c1RTYzRlk4ZWJVNmt6bGlJbGg3cHR4YXMyS2Y4Z2hDN1hRQmxjRFJqNG9QVQ?oc=5)). No post-election filing appears in today's leads.
- **Administration:** the Washington Post reports Trump said he will accept the results ([WaPo](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxOc1hPeURNaEZfaUMwRHFTakVWSFJtemZQSkJjd1FBOTZtQ1U5enZvdzRqVm5kOFdadzU1YzFjQjhVeVFBM1VMcnZncmlEdVBwbG93cDhWVFZqM0lHclhnekNHMTNyS0tneTBWYkl5bzRLRVgwTzBWX1NiaEVBRUl2ODFDVVV1c2d4MFV3LU9FRXdpbGducmZlRTRtbmlwYl9rd0NGN2JOdDN3dUd6LVpmZDRkODhRTDNwSUdkT3NLeElGV0U?oc=5)). NBC4 reports Vice President Vance blamed the Iran war for Republican losses ([NBC4](https://news.google.?oc=5)).

## What voters said
- **Exit polls (surveys):** NBC News's exit poll found many voters saw the election as a rebuke of Trump ([NBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxQcDQyYlg2UzJDSGdEYmNabGZWUXRYQlNXcFVXVW0taGpzeHA3R1RHSlRXUHkwcEJURlF2bTVGVkd2cVBhRm9iSkNQOWFuTDRkVUp6T2x0UDFaSF9DZmNYYTR5OUpCcDFkcVdUWmM5OWhVR1FJU0ZuVGRDUXVsVzkza3gtZHVuNEM4VHJxQS1tbXpFaTJjZElJQzhRYnhBOGRMRHZ6b09aSzhkdVZYR3c?oc=5)). NPR breaks down how Latino and young voters, among other groups, moved toward Democrats ([NPR](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxNd29ncDlIbmNIYzFHRWhGd215LTQ2eXpIUWZkOFFITGhKYi1UOUFpYkdVempuS0diSms3TF9ZUkgzRUhsUGRiOFNfamFfNHBXVGhMeFVwNl9iYVNJOF9lZU1hZGh0VTdxVEtucVllR1k5Ni1QWFBOQXJKemFNNFQzZmx3eWw?oc=5)).
- **North Carolina (Michael Bitzer):** two-thirds of the Senate vote came before Election Day and split about 64-35 for the Democrat. Republicans' early-vote share, 26%, was their worst since 2004, and every one of the state's 100 counties shifted toward Democrats. Bitzer says voter-history data will be needed to tell who turned out ([Center for NC Politics](https://ncpoliticscenter.substack.com/p/a-historic-bloodbath)).
- **Nevada:** The Nevada Independent's staff takeaways point to historic Democratic wins and slow counting ([Nevada Independent](https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/a-blue-bloodbath-10-big-takeaways-from-nevadas-2026-midterms/)). No Ralston voter-file read is in today's leads.
- **Who turned out:** the NYT breaks down the vote by race, gender, age and education ([NYT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxPM1Jxc0lSUzI0NVB6SGd3d0tlX2R1akVfdmR6ejBVcndPNTFkNS1EQ1ZkNmJsRGh1bHZjZmlzeW0ySjRxcnpuY1FNY0RncVBwX2J3SmRzaGZGUFRUaG5ndEdhLWo0VVdTQmI1SHFqLTJxUkhSZUhIekNpN3FqOHhYV09fRQ?oc=5)).
